title: File exceeds 1000 lines (2682 lines total)
detail: The file contains 2682 lines, well above the 1000-line maintainability threshold. The file defines the entire Nova exception hierarchy in a single module. Files of this size are hard to navigate, slow CI linting passes, and make it difficult for reviewers to reason about which exceptions are related. Suggested fix: split into sub-modules (e.g. nova/exceptions/compute.py, nova/exceptions/network.py) grouped by subsystem.

title: Broad `except Exception` in NovaException.__init__ swallows formatting errors
detail: Line 85 catches the base `Exception` to handle a failed `%`-interpolation of `msg_fmt`. While the intent is to fall back gracefully on a formatting bug, catching `Exception` masks every possible error including programming mistakes outside the message formatting. The fallback calls `self._log_exception()` and continues, so the original error type is lost. Suggested fix: catch only `KeyError` and `TypeError` — the only exceptions that `%`-formatting can plausibly raise.

title: 59 `super(ClassName, self)` calls use Python 2-style super()
detail: Throughout exception.py, every `super()` call passes explicit class and instance arguments (e.g. `super(NovaException, self).__init__(message)`), a Python 2 idiom that is redundant in Python 3. While not a defect, it adds noise and suggests the codebase has not been fully modernised. First occurrence: line 55. Suggested fix: replace with zero-argument `super().__init__(...)`.
